headline: Whale populations surge off southern Africa
meta_description: Antarctic blue whales and fin whales are making a remarkable comeback off southern Africa, with 95% of sightings recorded since 2012.
summary_short: A dramatic recovery is underway for whale populations off southern Africa, driven by steadily increasing sightings of Antarctic blue whales and fin whales.
body:
Whale populations are making a remarkable recovery off the coasts of southern Africa. Researchers tracking the animals have documented that 95% of all recorded sightings of Antarctic blue whales and fin whales in the region have occurred since 2012—a concentration that signals a genuine resurgence rather than random chance.

The steady climb in sightings suggests these whales are returning to waters they once inhabited, reversing decades of decline from industrial whaling. The data reflects not just occasional encounters, but a consistent upward trend that researchers say points to real population growth in the region.

This recovery offers a rare conservation victory, demonstrating that marine protection efforts and reduced hunting pressure can allow even the largest creatures on Earth to rebuild their numbers.
quick_facts: 95% of Antarctic blue and fin whale sightings off southern Africa since 2012
Whale populations recovering in southern African waters
Sightings steadily increasing over past decade
